candidates.summary: the realm cap truncates directly-changed realms, and the posted comment still links every one of them
candidates.failure_scenario: A repo-wide gno version bump edits every examples/**/gnomod.toml, which renderRelevant() counts as render-relevant. BuildPlan collects 58 changed realms, sorts changed-first, then `realms = realms[:maxRealms]` cuts to 25, so plan.Dirs (what gnodev is handed) holds 25. Comment() then writes one bullet per p.ChangedRealms, unfiltered, so all 58 get a clickable preview link and 33 of them 404. The same comment closes with '33 more affected realm(s) were not rendered (cap reached) - the changed realms are always kept', which is false for those 33.
candidates.verify_by: cp reviews/.../tests/b10-catalog-cap-drops-changed-realms.go misc/gnopreview/zz_b10_cap_test.go && cd misc/gnopreview && GNOROOT_FIXTURE=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) go test -run TestB10 -v .
candidates.evidence: ChangedRealms=58 rendered=25 Dropped=33 / changed realms linked but never rendered (404): 33 / comment length=13436 bytes, bullet lines=58 / comment claims 'changed realms are always kept': true. Synthetic case: ChangedRealms=[a b c], Realms=[a b], Dirs=[examples/gno.land/r/x/a examples/gno.land/r/x/b], comment links https://example.test/pr-1/r/x/c/.

candidates.summary: the 'quarantined packages never appear' case pins nothing: the pkgRoot prefix guard can be deleted and it stays green
candidates.failure_scenario: The case feeds examples/quarantined/gno.land/r/x/quar/lib.gno and expects no realms. LoadPkgs only walks examples/gno.land, so byDir has no entry for that directory and the file is dropped by the `p != nil` lookup whatever the prefix guard does. Deleting `!strings.HasPrefix(f, pkgRoot+"/")` from BuildPlan leaves `go test -run TestBuildPlan .` green, so the guard the case is named for is unprotected: a later refactor that also widens LoadPkgs would start previewing quarantined packages with no test to say so.
candidates.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && perl -0pi -e 's/if !strings\.HasPrefix\(f, pkgRoot\+"\/"\) \|\| !renderRelevant\(f\) \{/if !renderRelevant(f) {/' plan.go && go test -run TestBuildPlan .

candidates.summary: the only cap case keeps one changed realm under a cap of one, so changed-realms-over-cap is never exercised
candidates.failure_scenario: 'cap keeps the changed realm and reports the rest' sets maxRealms=1 with exactly one changed realm (r/x/other) and one indirect (r/x/leaf), so the stable changed-first partition alone decides the result and the truncation never cuts into the changed group. The bound the case is named for - changed realms are always kept - has no case where len(ChangedRealms) > maxRealms, which is the shape that ships the 33 dead links above.
candidates.verify_by: add a case with three changed realms and maxRealms=2 and assert every ChangedRealms entry is in Realms; see TestB10CapDropsDirectlyChangedRealms in the repro file
candidates.evidence: TestB10CapDropsDirectlyChangedRealms: ChangedRealms=[gno.land/r/x/a gno.land/r/x/b gno.land/r/x/c], Realms(rendered)=[gno.land/r/x/a gno.land/r/x/b], Dropped=1

candidates.summary: fakeRepo builds an `ignore = true` package but no case changes a file inside it, so the `!p.Ignore` guard on a direct change is untested
candidates.failure_scenario: Every case reaches examples/gno.land/r/x/ignored only through the indirect path, where a second filter (`pkgs[p].Ignore` in the affected loop) already excludes it. Deleting `&& !p.Ignore` from the changed-file lookup in BuildPlan leaves `go test -run TestBuildPlan .` green. If that guard is ever lost, a directly changed ignored realm enters ChangedRealms - and so gets a comment link - while the affected loop still keeps it out of Realms and Dirs, producing the same 404 link as the cap defect.
candidates.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && perl -0pi -e 's/if p := byDir\[path\.Dir\(f\)\]; p != nil && !p\.Ignore \{/if p := byDir[path.Dir(f)]; p != nil {/' plan.go && go test -run TestBuildPlan .

candidates.summary: 'tests fixtures are not pulled in indirectly' cannot reach the fixture it names, so indirectExclude is pinned only by the case above it
candidates.failure_scenario: The case changes examples/gno.land/p/x/mid/v0/lib.gno, but fakeRepo's r/tests/vm/fixture imports p/x/base/v0, not p/x/mid/v0, so the fixture is not in mid's dependent set under any rule. Deleting the indirectExclude filter turns 'transitive dependency pulls both dependents' red and leaves this case green; a maintainer trimming the transitive case as redundant would silently lose the only coverage of the r/tests/ exclusion.

candidates.summary: Pkg.Draft is parsed and stored and never read, and no plan_test case covers `draft = true`
candidates.failure_scenario: modFlags returns both flags and BuildPlan assigns pkg.Draft, but nothing in misc/gnopreview ever reads the field, so it is dead state that reads as a policy the tool does not have. Previewing a draft realm is in fact correct - gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:668 rejects a draft addpkg only above height 0, so gnodev's genesis loads examples/gno.land/r/demo/draftrealm - which makes the field removable rather than a missing filter.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rn 'Draft' misc/gnopreview/*.go  (one declaration, one assignment, no read)
candidates.evidence: plan.go:58 declaration, plan.go:142 assignment, no other hit in the package

candidates.summary: the gnoweb seed realms are appended after the truncation, so maxRealms is not a bound on len(plan.Realms)
candidates.failure_scenario: BuildPlan truncates to maxRealms, sets plan.Dropped, then appends up to four gnowebSeedRealms that were not already kept, so a gnoweb-touching PR can hand gnodev up to maxRealms+4 realms while the comment still reports Dropped against the pre-seed count. The overrun is small and I could not exhibit it on the real repo: with all 145 gnomod.toml files plus a gnoweb change, the four seeds were already inside the kept 25 and len(Realms)=25.
candidates.verify_by: build a fake repo whose 25 changed realms sort before gno.land/r/docs/security_patterns, set Gnoweb, and assert len(plan.Realms) <= maxRealms
candidates.evidence: TestSeedsOverflowTheCap on the real tree: maxRealms=25 len(Realms)=25 len(Dirs)=25 Dropped=33 - no overflow exhibited, the append-after-truncate shape is read-only evidence

candidates.summary: modFlags swallows the gnomod.toml read error and reports draft=false, ignore=false
candidates.failure_scenario: LoadPkgs only calls modFlags once it has seen a gnomod.toml entry in the directory, so the read failing means a permission change or a concurrent removal between ReadDir and ReadFile. In that window an `ignore = true` package is silently treated as live and gets rendered and linked. Thin reachability; the fix is to return the error or log it rather than collapse it into two falses.
candidates.verify_by: chmod 000 examples/gno.land/r/x/<pkg>/gnomod.toml as a non-root user, run BuildPlan on that root, observe the package present in plan.Realms
candidates.evidence: plan.go:155-159 returns false,false on any os.ReadFile error
